FULL EXPERIMENT DESIGN (design-only; no experiment run, no results claimed)

═══════════════════════════════════════════
0. FIXED REQUIREMENTS (from researcher)
═══════════════════════════════════════════
• Exactly two source-supported arms: A1 = SiT with original time attention (control); A2 = SiT with the time-attention mechanism replaced by a non-causal Hyena operator (treatment). These are fixed by the source; everything else below is my design choice and is labeled [DESIGN CHOICE] where it is not forced by the task statement.
• Design-only deliverable. All outcomes framed as predictions, never findings.

═══════════════════════════════════════════
1. MODEL AND COMPARISON-ARM SPECIFICATION
═══════════════════════════════════════════
1.1 Base architecture [DESIGN CHOICE]
SiT (Scalable Interpolant Transformers) video variant: a DiT-style transformer over spatiotemporal patch tokens, with (i) self-attention over spatial tokens within each frame block, and (ii) a "time attention" mechanism operating across the diffusion-time axis — i.e., the axis indexing the trajectory frames/steps that a single denoising step conditions on. The control arm A1 keeps this module exactly as in the reference implementation. Model scale: the smallest configuration that learns the chosen dataset reliably (see §2), to keep matched-compute training feasible; exact scale is parameterized, not fixed, because no source prescription exists.

1.2 Treatment arm A2 — Hyena replacement [DESIGN CHOICE, constrained by the fixed statement "replace the time attention mechanism"]
• Which blocks: every block in which the original time attention operates (the temporal mixing sublayers only). Spatial self-attention, MLPs, adaLN conditioning, patch embedding, and the interpolant training objective are untouched. This isolates the effect of the temporal operator.
• Operator: non-causal Hyena (long explicit/implicit convolution with data-controlled gating: y_t = Σ_k K_Δ(t, k) · gates; implemented as an FFT convolution over the diffusion-time axis with exponential-modulation kernels and a diagonal, data-dependent gating MLP, per the Hyena/HyenaDNA design). Non-causality is standard for non-autoregressive diffusion and is fixed by the question statement.
• Position encoding over the diffusion-time axis — the ordering-vs-set semantics issue, resolved and justified: SiT's time axis indexes the trajectory's temporal frames, which are ordered in physical time (frame 1 occurs before frame 2), even though the model processes them as a set-like token block in parallel. I adopt the ORDERED interpretation: positions are the frames' physical time indices on a regular grid, encoded with Hyena's implicit position encoding (learned sinusoidal-style embedding z_t of position, conditioning the kernel K(z_t, z_{t−k})). Justification: (a) the hypothesis is about trajectory dynamics over physical time, so temporal ordering is the inductive bias we deliberately inject and test; (b) Hyena's length-generalization via implicit kernels depends on continuous position encoding, which only has the intended meaning under the ordered interpretation; (c) the "set" interpretation would discard the very structure the hypothesis is about, making the experiment uninformative. This is the single most consequential conceptual choice in the design and is documented as Assumption AU-1 (§5).
• Parameter/FLOP matching strategy: (i) primary match — total trainable parameters within ±2% between A1 and A2, achieved by tuning the Hyena channel-expansion width (the gating MLP width) and filter-order projection dimensions; time-attention layers are typically a small fraction of DiT parameters, so the Hyena branch is width-scaled to absorb the difference; (ii) secondary reporting — per-step training FLOPs and wall-clock per 1k steps for both arms, reported openly (exact parity is not forced; matched optimization budget in steps is, i.e., both arms train for the identical number of steps and samples seen). Learning rate and schedule are tuned once per arm on a short proxy run with identical budget, then frozen.

1.3 A3 — scaled-attention control [SUGGESTED ADDITION, clearly optional]
A third arm: the original time attention with position encodings extended/interpolated (e.g., RoPE-style frequency scaling) to the long generation length at inference, and optionally fine-tuned briefly at an intermediate length. Purpose: to separate the hypothesis "Hyena's receptive field/implicit kernels generalize in length" from the trivial confound "attention with rescaled positions also generalizes." If budget allows, A3 is trained at the same cost as A1/A2; if not, A3 runs only at inference-time adaptation from the A1 checkpoint. It is NOT required for the hypothesis test; omitting it weakens interpretation but not validity of the A1-vs-A2 comparison.

═══════════════════════════════════════════
2. DATASET AND OPERATIONAL DEFINITIONS
═══════════════════════════════════════════
2.1 Dataset [DESIGN CHOICE]
Primary: 2D Kolmogorov-flow / forced incompressible Navier–Stokes simulation data (or equivalently the PDE-bench-style turbulence trajectory sets). Justification: it exhibits cleanly separated timescales — a slow, coherent large-scale vortex/energy-envelope dynamics and fast small-scale vortical fluctuations — with an exact ground truth available for arbitrarily long rollouts from a cheap reference solver, so spectral ground truth at any length is available without annotation. Secondary (robustness check): a multiscale ODE system (e.g., Lorenz-96 two-tier, F = fast variables coupled to X = slow variables), which is cheap enough to run the full protocol many times and provides analytic timescale separation (slow mode decay times vs. fast oscillation periods). Training set: trajectories of length L_train frames, sampled from long simulations; held-out set: longer trajectories from the same simulator for evaluation up to the maximum evaluated length.
Trajectory representation for SiT: frames are the "time axis"; each frame's spatial field is patchified as in the base SiT video model.

2.2 "Extremely long" [operational definition]
A generated trajectory of length L_gen such that L_gen = r · L_train with r ∈ {1, 2, 4, 8} evaluated systematically, plus a search upward in ×2 steps until the failure criterion (§3.2) triggers. "Extremely long" concretely means r ≥ 4 with full metrics reported at every r. The length-generalization claim is evaluated at generation time only: both arms are trained exclusively at L_train; no length curriculum, no length conditioning changes (if the base SiT uses any length embedding, both arms share it identically).

2.3 "Consistency" [operational definition, three layers]
C1 — Per-frame quality across the rollout: per-frame FID/KID-style distributional distance (or field-space RMSE in physical units for PDE data) computed in non-overlapping windows along the trajectory; a trajectory is consistent if the windowed metric does not degrade by more than a pre-registered tolerance (e.g., median window metric stays within 1.5× its value over the first window, for windows covering ≥80% of L_gen). This turns "no degradation along the rollout" into a falsifiable criterion rather than an average.
C2 — Temporal coherence / no drift or collapse: (a) rolling-window FVD (video datasets) or windowed two-sample statistics on field statistics (energy, enstrophy, vorticity histograms for PDE data) — flatness of these statistics over time is required; (b) feature-persistence: correlation of a fixed object/structure descriptor between consecutive windows (e.g., dominant vortex positions for Kolmogorov flow) must not decay to chance level; (c) drift metric: absolute difference between first-window and last-window summary statistics.
C3 — Trajectory-level distributional match: FVD (or the PDE analogue: distributional distance over trajectory-level statistics) between generated sets of length-L_gen trajectories and ground-truth sets of the same length.

2.4 "Multi-timescale dynamics" [operational definition]
M1 — Band-resolved spectral fidelity: per-trajectory power spectral density (2D field spectra time-resolved, or 1D temporal spectra per spatial mode); compare generated vs. ground truth separately in a LOW band (frequencies below the characteristic slow-mode frequency) and a HIGH band (above it), via band-integrated spectral RMSE and log-spectral distance. The two-scale claim requires BOTH bands to match within tolerance; success in only one band is reported as partial.
M2 — Lagged correlation structure: auto-/cross-correlation functions of key observables (e.g., large-scale vorticity mode for the slow timescale; a high-wave-number energy proxy for the fast timescale) compared between generated and true trajectories; metric = integrated L1 difference of the correlation curves, reported per lag band so short-lag (fast) and long-lag (slow) fidelity are separately visible.
M3 — Timescale extraction: fitted characteristic timescales (e.g., decay time of the slow mode's autocorrelation, mean period of the fast oscillation) from generated vs. true trajectories; report relative error per timescale. This gives an interpretable, one-number-per-timescale summary.

═══════════════════════════════════════════
3. TRAINING AND EVALUATION PROTOCOL
═══════════════════════════════════════════
3.1 Training [matched compute]
• Both arms trained on identical data order (shared seed), identical batch size, identical number of optimizer steps, identical interpolant/flow objective and sampler schedule.
• Optimization budget parity: identical step count and samples seen; FLOP differences reported, not equalized (see §5).
• LR/schedule tuned on short proxy runs per arm under identical proxy budget; then frozen for the full run.
• ≥3 seeds per arm (3 minimum; 5 preferred) for error bars on every headline metric.

3.2 Evaluation
• Generate N ≥ 256 trajectories per arm per evaluated length r ∈ {1, 2, 4, 8, …} with identical samplers/steps.
• Failure criterion (defines the generation-length limit): the smallest evaluated r at which C1 tolerance is violated, or C2 shows drift beyond threshold, or trajectory-level C3 degrades beyond a pre-registered margin. Report the limit curve — generation-length limit as a function of arm.
• All metrics (§2.3, §2.4) computed at every evaluated r; paired comparisons arm-by-arm at each r.
• Hyena ablation (A2 only): sweep kernel filter order (e.g., 2, 4, 8) and effective kernel length/positional-encoding frequency range; measure whether the generation-length limit and long-lag correlation fidelity scale with the operator's receptive field, holding parameters matched per A2-config. Purpose: test the mechanism (receptive-field-driven length generalization), not just the end-to-end score.

3.3 Statistical treatment
• Metric comparisons at each r: paired-by-seed mean ± std, plus a distributional two-sample test on trajectory-level metrics; pre-registered tolerances (from §2.3) fixed before any generation run.

═══════════════════════════════════════════
4. ANALYSIS PLAN — DECISION CRITERIA
═══════════════════════════════════════════
The hypothesis is SUPPORTED only if ALL of the following hold (with seed-level error bars, paired across seeds):
 (i) Length: A2's generation-length limit ≥ A1's limit by at least one evaluated doubling step (r = 4 or beyond for A2), with A1 failing at or before r = 2 under the same criteria; or, if both arms pass all r, A2 shows no degradation where A1 does.
 (ii) Consistency: at every evaluated r where both arms pass, A2's C1/C2/C3 metrics are statistically non-inferior to A1's (non-inferiority margin pre-registered, e.g., 10% relative); if A1 fails first, A2's metrics remain inside tolerance at the larger r.
 (iii) Multi-timescale: A2's M1 band-integrated spectral errors and M2 lagged-correlation differences are non-inferior to A1's in BOTH bands, and M3 relative errors of extracted timescales are comparable or better for both slow and fast timescales.
The hypothesis is REFUTED if A2 is non-inferior on at most one of (i)/(ii)/(iii), or fails earlier than A1 on the length-limit criterion, or shows spectral fidelity in only one band (indicating it captures one timescale but not multi-timescale structure).
A MIXED result (e.g., equal length limits but A2 better on long-lag correlation) is reported as such — the design pre-registers the primary criterion as the conjunction of (i)–(iii), so no post-hoc re-interpretation is needed.
Fairness controls: matched parameters/steps/schedule/sampler; identical data seeds; identical evaluation code path; A3 (if run) isolates operator type from position-scaling effects; the Hyena ablation ties any observed gain to receptive field rather than parameter placement.

Predictions (explicitly predictions, not findings): if Hyena's implicit-kernel length extrapolation transfers to the diffusion-time axis, A2 should degrade more gracefully at r ≥ 4 and maintain long-lag correlation structure better; if the diffusion-time axis's ordered semantics are mis-specified or the interpolation objective does not exercise the long receptive field, both arms should behave similarly and the hypothesis would be refuted. These are stated as expectations to be tested, with no claimed outcome.

═══════════════════════════════════════════
5. FEASIBILITY AND ASSUMPTIONS
═══════════════════════════════════════════
5.1 Cost accounting (feasibility)
• Attention over the diffusion-time axis costs O(L²·d) at sequence length L (number of trajectory frames processed per denoising step); non-causal Hyena costs O(L log L) FFT convolution + O(L·d) gating. For small L (training, L_train frames, typically tens to a few hundred), attention is cheap and Hyena's FFT overhead means A2 may train slower per step — hence step-count parity, with FLOP/wall-clock parity reported but not forced. For long L (generation at r = 8+), Hyena's advantage grows; generation cost at extreme lengths favors A2, which should be reported as a practical benefit separate from the quality hypothesis.
• Memory: attention materializes L² score maps (or flash-attention reduces memory but not asymptotics); Hyena needs O(L) activations plus FFT workspace. Feasible on single-node multi-GPU for the proposed scales; the design keeps model scale minimal deliberately.
• Engineering risk: Hyena's FFT convolution over a non-standard axis (frame axis within a DiT token grid) requires careful reshaping and may need a custom kernel; a fallback is a long-convolution implementation in PyTorch FFT primitives, which is sufficient for design-scale experiments.

5.2 The length-extrapolation mechanism question
The core mechanism being tested is Hyena's ability to generalize beyond training sequence length via implicit, continuously-parameterized position encodings (as demonstrated in HyenaDNA-style settings), whereas softmax attention with learned/rotary positions typically degrades beyond training length. The design makes this the explicit object of measurement (the r-sweep and the A3 scaled-attention control). Key open risk: it is not established from the source that the diffusion-time axis in SiT is even treated as a length-extrapolatable sequence — if the reference implementation conditions on diffusion time in a way that is invariant to trajectory length (e.g., fixed-size frame blocks), the "generation length" manipulation must be defined at the frame-block level, and this definition is [DESIGN CHOICE] documented below.

5.3 Explicit assumptions section
Assumptions (design choices I make, not source-supported claims):
 AS-1: The base model is a SiT video/dynamics variant whose "time attention" mixes information across the trajectory-frame (diffusion-time) axis; its exact layer placement follows the standard DiT-block layout (time attention as an additional temporal sublayer alongside spatial attention). No source specifies otherwise.
 AS-2: Ordered (not set) semantics for the diffusion-time axis, for the reasons in §1.2 — the central conceptual assumption (AU-1).
 AS-3: Dataset is Kolmogorov-flow/Navier–Stokes simulation data (primary) + Lorenz-96 (secondary); chosen for clean timescale separation and cheap ground truth. Not source-prescribed.
 AS-4: Matched-parameter (±2%) and matched-step training; FLOP/wall-clock parity reported, not enforced.
 AS-5: Model scale, tolerance thresholds, r-grid, seed count, and sample counts are chosen to make the protocol feasible on a modest single-node compute budget; they are parameters, not prescriptions, and would be scaled up if the compute budget were larger.
 AS-6: Non-causal (bidirectional) kernels are used, per the question statement; causality is irrelevant because the diffusion-time axis is not autoregressive.
Uncertainties (cannot be resolved from the source; flagged, handled by design):
 AU-1: Diffusion-time-axis semantics (ordered vs. set) — resolved by assumption AS-2 with justification; if the researcher's intent differs, the position-encoding design and interpretation of "long trajectory" change.
 AU-2: Exact paper integration details and prescribed Hyena hyperparameters are unavailable; kernel order/width are swept in the ablation rather than fixed.
 AU-3: Compute budget unspecified; the protocol is sized to be modestly feasible and reports costs so it can be rescaled.
 AU-4: Whether length generalization should be tested at training time (curriculum) or only at inference; design assumes inference-only extrapolation (strictest and most informative test).
 AU-5: Whether "consistency" should be judged distributionally or per-trajectory; the design uses both (C1/C2 per-trajectory windowed, C3 distributional).
 AU-6: Hyena position-encoding frequency range must cover the evaluated generation lengths; if it does not, apparent length generalization could be an artifact of encoding range — handled by evaluating at lengths within and beyond the encoding range and reporting both.

Deliverable status: this is a complete design specification. No code was run, no model was trained, no trajectories were generated, and no results exist; all outcome statements are framed as pre-registered predictions and decision criteria.

A generated trajectory of length L_gen such that L_gen = r · L_train with r ∈ {1, 2, 4, 8} evaluated systematically, plus a search upward in ×2 steps until the failure criterion (§3.2) triggers. "Extremely long" concretely means r ≥ 4 with full metrics reported at every r. The length-generalization claim is evaluated at generation time only: both arms are trained exclusively at L_train; no length curriculum, no length conditioning changes (if the base SiT uses any length embedding, both arms share it identically).

2.3 "Consistency" [operational definition, three layers]
C1 — Per-frame quality across the rollout: per-frame FID/KID-style distributional distance (or field-space RMSE in physical units for PDE data) computed in non-overlapping windows along the trajectory; a trajectory is consistent if the windowed metric does not degrade by more than a pre-registered tolerance (e.g., median window metric stays within 1.5× its value over the first window, for windows covering ≥80% of L_gen). This turns "no degradation along the rollout" into a falsifiable criterion rather than an average.
C2 — Temporal coherence / no drift or collapse: (a) rolling-window FVD (video datasets) or windowed two-sample statistics on field statistics (energy, enstrophy, vorticity histograms for PDE data) — flatness of these statistics over time is required; (b) feature-persistence: correlation of a fixed object/structure descriptor between consecutive windows (e.g., dominant vortex positions for Kolmogorov flow) must not decay to chance level; (c) drift metric: absolute difference between first-window and last-window summary statistics.
C3 — Trajectory-level distributional match: FVD (or the PDE analogue: distributional distance over trajectory-level statistics) between generated sets of length-L_gen trajectories and ground-truth sets of the same length.

2.4 "Multi-timescale dynamics" [operational definition]
M1 — Band-resolved spectral fidelity: per-trajectory power spectral density (2D field spectra time-resolved, or 1D temporal spectra per spatial mode); compare generated vs. ground truth separately in a LOW band (frequencies below the characteristic slow-mode frequency) and a HIGH band (above it), via band-integrated spectral RMSE and log-spectral distance. The two-scale claim requires BOTH bands to match within tolerance; success in only one band is reported as partial.
M2 — Lagged correlation structure: auto-/cross-correlation functions of key observables (e.g., large-scale vorticity mode for the slow timescale; a high-wave-number energy proxy for the fast timescale) compared between generated and true trajectories; metric = integrated L1 difference of the correlation curves, reported per lag band so short-lag (fast) and long-lag (slow) fidelity are separately visible.
M3 — Timescale extraction: fitted characteristic timescales (e.g., decay time of the slow mode's autocorrelation, mean period of the fast oscillation) from generated vs. true trajectories; report relative error per timescale. This gives an interpretable, one-number-per-timescale summary.

═══════════════════════════════════════════
3. TRAINING AND EVALUATION PROTOCOL
═══════════════════════════════════════════
3.1 Training [matched compute]
• Both arms trained on identical data order (shared seed), identical batch size, identical number of optimizer steps, identical interpolant/flow objective and sampler schedule.
• Optimization budget parity: identical step count and samples seen; FLOP differences reported, not equalized (see §5).
• LR/schedule tuned on short proxy runs per arm under identical proxy budget; then frozen for the full run.
• ≥3 seeds per arm (3 minimum; 5 preferred) for error bars on every headline metric.

3.2 Evaluation
• Generate N ≥ 256 trajectories per arm per evaluated length r ∈ {1, 2, 4, 8, …} with identical samplers/steps.
• Failure criterion (defines the generation-length limit): the smallest evaluated r at which C1 tolerance is violated, or C2 shows drift beyond threshold, or trajectory-level C3 degrades beyond a pre-registered margin. Report the limit curve — generation-length limit as a function of arm.
• All metrics (§2.3, §2.4) computed at every evaluated r; paired comparisons arm-by-arm at each r.
• Hyena ablation (A2 only): sweep kernel filter order (e.g., 2, 4, 8) and effective kernel length/positional-encoding frequency range; measure whether the generation-length limit and long-lag correlation fidelity scale with the operator's receptive field, holding parameters matched per A2-config. Purpose: test the mechanism (receptive-field-driven length generalization), not just the end-to-end score.

3.3 Statistical treatment
• Metric comparisons at each r: paired-by-seed mean ± std, plus a distributional two-sample test on trajectory-level metrics; pre-registered tolerances (from §2.3) fixed before any generation run.

4. ANALYSIS PLAN — DECISION CRITERIA
═══════════════════════════════════════════
The hypothesis is SUPPORTED only if ALL of the following hold (with seed-level error bars, paired across seeds):
 (i) Length: A2's generation-length limit ≥ A1's limit by at least one evaluated doubling step (r = 4 or beyond for A2), with A1 failing at or before r = 2 under the same criteria; or, if both arms pass all r, A2 shows no degradation where A1 does.
 (ii) Consistency: at every evaluated r where both arms pass, A2's C1/C2/C3 metrics are statistically non-inferior to A1's (non-inferiority margin pre-registered, e.g., 10% relative); if A1 fails first, A2's metrics remain inside tolerance at the larger r.
 (iii) Multi-timescale: A2's M1 band-integrated spectral errors and M2 lagged-correlation differences are non-inferior to A1's in BOTH bands, and M3 relative errors of extracted timescales are comparable or better for both slow and fast timescales.
The hypothesis is REFUTED if A2 is non-inferior on at most one of (i)/(ii)/(iii), or fails earlier than A1 on the length-limit criterion, or shows spectral fidelity in only one band (indicating it captures one timescale but not multi-timescale structure).
A MIXED result (e.g., equal length limits but A2 better on long-lag correlation) is reported as such — the design pre-registers the primary criterion as the conjunction of (i)–(iii), so no post-hoc re-interpretation is needed.
Fairness controls: matched parameters/steps/schedule/sampler; identical data seeds; identical evaluation code path; A3 (if run) isolates operator type from position-scaling effects; the Hyena ablation ties any observed gain to receptive field rather than parameter placement.

Predictions (explicitly predictions, not findings): if Hyena's implicit-kernel length extrapolation transfers to the diffusion-time axis, A2 should degrade more gracefully at r ≥ 4 and maintain long-lag correlation structure better; if the diffusion-time axis's ordered semantics are mis-specified or the interpolation objective does not exercise the long receptive field, both arms should behave similarly and the hypothesis would be refuted. These are stated as expectations to be tested, with no claimed outcome.

5. FEASIBILITY AND ASSUMPTIONS
═══════════════════════════════════════════
5.1 Cost accounting (feasibility)
• Attention over the diffusion-time axis costs O(L²·d) at sequence length L (number of trajectory frames processed per denoising step); non-causal Hyena costs O(L log L) FFT convolution + O(L·d) gating. For small L (training, L_train frames, typically tens to a few hundred), attention is cheap and Hyena's FFT overhead means A2 may train slower per step — hence step-count parity, with FLOP/wall-clock parity reported but not forced. For long L (generation at r = 8+), Hyena's advantage grows; generation cost at extreme lengths favors A2, which should be reported as a practical benefit separate from the quality hypothesis.
• Memory: attention materializes L² score maps (or flash-attention reduces memory but not asymptotics); Hyena needs O(L) activations plus FFT workspace. Feasible on single-node multi-GPU for the proposed scales; the design keeps model scale minimal deliberately.
• Engineering risk: Hyena's FFT convolution over a non-standard axis (frame axis within a DiT token grid) requires careful reshaping and may need a custom kernel; a fallback is a long-convolution implementation in PyTorch FFT primitives, which is sufficient for design-scale experiments.

5.2 The length-extrapolation mechanism question
The core mechanism being tested is Hyena's ability to generalize beyond training sequence length via implicit, continuously-parameterized position encodings (as demonstrated in HyenaDNA-style settings), whereas softmax attention with learned/rotary positions typically degrades beyond training length. The design makes this the explicit object of measurement (the r-sweep and the A3 scaled-attention control). Key open risk: it is not established from the source that the diffusion-time axis in SiT is even treated as a length-extrapolatable sequence — if the reference implementation conditions on diffusion time in a way that is invariant to trajectory length (e.g., fixed-size frame blocks), the "generation length" manipulation must be defined at the frame-block level, and this definition is [DESIGN CHOICE] documented below.

5.3 Explicit assumptions section
Assumptions (design choices I make, not source-supported claims):

No source specifies otherwise.
 AS-2: Ordered (not set) semantics for the diffusion-time axis, for the reasons in §1.2 — the central conceptual assumption (AU-1).
 AS-3: Dataset is Kolmogorov-flow/Navier–Stokes simulation data (primary) + Lorenz-96 (secondary); chosen for clean timescale separation and cheap ground truth. Not source-prescribed.

Uncertainties (cannot be resolved from the source; flagged, handled by design):
